tools.name: recall_repository_memory
tools.description: Recall verified behavioral contracts before changing a repository. Returns claims, scope, provenance, boundaries and regression hashes.

change.description: The proposed code change or behavior being investigated.

repository.description: Optional repository key used to restrict recall.

semantic.description: Use budgeted embedding recall when authorized.

instructions: Treat claims as behavioral constraints, not implementation instructions.
Do not modify or expose the frozen regression; request a server-side replay.
If the intended contract changed, supersede the memory with reviewed evidence.

memories.claim: On Windows, safe_join currently accepts special device filenames such as CON and NUL. It should return None for Windows special device names, while preserving ordinary joins and traversal rejection. Do not open any Windows device; this is string validation only. Tests execute on Linux: emulate the Windows branch by replacing the target module-local os reference (werkzeug.security.os) with a SimpleNamespace(name="nt", path=posixpath), without changing the global os module. Without Windows emulation, CON remains an ordinary Linux filename and must still be accepted.
risk_boundaries: Checks cover the collected tests, not universal correctness.
Untrusted Python can manipulate its own test framework; evidence is not adversarial proof.
Dependencies use published binary wheels only. Native source builds and system-package recipes require a separately prepared image.
invalidated_when: The recorded behavioral contract intentionally changes.
The frozen regression no longer represents the public behavior.
The recorded environment is no longer reproducible.
